Jasmine / Laura — ops input below (keeping it actionable):

Options for TechForge (short pros/cons):

A) Payer sends USD to Redwood US bank (recommended)\- Pros: No intermediary deductions at inbound leg; cleaner trace (MT103) so we can sweep into INR ourselves; predictable net amount.\- Cons: Buyer pays USD FX on their side.

B) Payer sends INR directly to Redwood India account\- Pros: Buyer handles FX; local INR finalization faster for their AP.\- Cons: Likely 1–2 intermediary banks; we frequently see £/USD->INR rails with correspondent fees that result in unknown deductions unless the sender includes full MT103 and instructs beneficiary pays (OUR) or sender covers charges (SHA vs OUR semantics).

Recommendation: Ask TechForge to either (1) pay USD to Redwood US nostro (option A) OR (2) if they must pay INR, provide full MT103 and explicitly select SHA=sender-pays-intermediary (but note SHA means fees can be split — ambiguity remains). Best practical approach is to request MT103 proof and have payer absorb intermediary fees, or request they call their bank to set 'BEN'/'OUR' as per Indian clearing rules (many banks won't support OUR).
